canonical_question: What are the specific SRIM parameters used to calculate the hardness contribution from Ar implantation?

question_variants.question: What are the specific SRIM parameters used to calculate the hardness contribution from Ar implantation?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text states SRIM was used with the Kinchin-Pease model and a 40 eV threshold, but specific parameters for calculating hardness contribution (beyond displacement threshold) are not detailed in the evidence.

answers.answer: The simulation used the Kinchin-Pease model in SRIM (version 2013) with a displacement threshold energy of 40 eV.
answers.conditions: 1-MeV Kr+2 and 16 keV He+ at 1173 K
answers.measurement_outcome: dpa and He implantation profiles calculated
answers.mechanism: SRIM Monte Carlo simulation using Kinchin-Pease model
answers.boundary_limitation: Specific hardness contribution parameters beyond displacement threshold not detailed
evidence_spans: The dpa and He implantation profiles were calculated using the Kinchin-Pease model in the Stopping & Range of Ions in Matter (SRIM) Monte Carlo computer simulation code (version 2013) [58] and 40 eV [59] was taken as the displacement threshold energy for all elements.
